title: What If a Skyscraper Melted Your Car? In 2013 London's Did

scenes.text: What if a skyscraper could melt your car? In 2013, one in London did.
The 37-storey tower has a curved glass face pointing south. It worked like a giant concave mirror.
For about two hours a day, it focused sunlight on one street. A Jaguar was parked there for about an hour.
Its mirror, badge and panels melted; the developers paid 946 pounds. Nearby, tiles cracked and someone fried an egg.
The architect had predicted 36 degrees Celsius. He said it turned out more like 72.
Sunshade fins now cover the glass. And his earlier hotel in Las Vegas had already scorched its own pool deck.

description:
What if a skyscraper melted your car? In late summer 2013 the concave, south-facing glass of London's 37-storey 20 Fenchurch Street, the Walkie-Talkie, focused sunlight onto the street for about two hours a day. A Jaguar XJ parked there for about an hour had its mirror, badge and panels melted, and the developers paid the 946 pound repair bill.
Shop tiles cracked, carpets were singed and someone fried an egg in the beam. Permanent sunshade fins were fitted to the facade. The same architect's Vdara hotel in Las Vegas had earlier focused sunlight on its pool deck.
